title: 2001 HMMT February Geometry Problem 10
statement: \(A\) is the center of a semicircle, with radius \(A D\) lying on the base. \(B\) lies on the base between \(A\) and \(D\), and \(E\) is on the circular portion of the semicircle such that \(E B A\) is a right angle. Extend \(E A\) through \(A\) to \(C\), and put \(F\) on line \(C D\) such that \(E B F\) is a line. Now \(E A=1, A C=\sqrt{2}, B F=\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{4}, C F=\frac{2 \sqrt{5}+\sqrt{10}}{4}\), and \(D F=\frac{2 \sqrt{5}-\sqrt{10}}{4}\). Find \(D E\).

solutions.text: Let \(\theta=\angle A E D\) and \(x=D E\). By the law of cosines on triangle \(A D E\), we have \(1=1+x^{2}-2 x \cos \theta \Rightarrow 2 x \cos \theta=x^{2}\). Then by the law of cosines on triangle \(C D E\) (note that \(C D=\sqrt{5})\), we have \(5=(1+\sqrt{2})^{2}+x^{2}-2(1+\sqrt{2}) x \cos \theta=(1+\sqrt{2})^{2}+x^{2}-(1+\sqrt{2}) x^{2}\). Solving the quadratic equation gives \(x=\sqrt{2-\sqrt{2}}\).
